analysis.title: Microsoft F1Q Preview - Twin engine turbo
key_insights: DB rates MSFT Buy and raises its price target to $600 from $550, about 28x CY27E EPS on its own estimates. The price was $535.07 on 9 Oct 2026.

DB expects a third straight quarter of faster constant-currency revenue growth with y/y operating margin expansion in F1Q27, driven by Azure and M365 Commercial Cloud on OpEx growth of about +MSD y/y.
Revenue is expected to decline y/y in the newly formed Devices & Consumer segment and in most license-based lines (Server Products, M365 Consumer Products, Industry Products, Windows OEM, Gaming).
Investors are likely to look for a couple points of topline outperformance, guidance that supports further acceleration through the year, and a reiteration that Microsoft stays FCF positive in FY27.
F1Q27 revenue guidance midpoint is $90.4bn, about +17% y/y at constant currency. DB expects results 1-2 points better, around +18%-19% y/y at constant currency.
Agents & Infra segment is guided to about +23% y/y at constant currency, a 1pt sequential acceleration. Devices & Consumer is guided to about -6.5% y/y at constant currency.

Gross margin is guided to 67.1% (-1.9pt y/y) on AI investment. DB thinks it ends nearer 68% with revenue upside. A change extending datacenter and building useful life to 25 years from 15 is a tailwind that management has not quantified beyond a 'minimal benefit' to FY27 operating income.
OpEx is guided to grow +7.5% y/y against revenue at +16%, for a -0.4pt y/y dip in operating margin. DB thinks this is conservative and operating margin can rise y/y.

Azure is guided +44-45% y/y at constant currency versus +42% in F4Q, implying net adds of about $2.8bn. DB sees +46% as a fair bogey, above the guidance range, and does not expect a repeat of last quarter's 3.5pt outperformance.
Azure is likely the most capacity-constrained major cloud provider near term because of 1P app demand and priority allocation to 1P Apps and R&D, ahead of Vera Rubin capacity starting in F2Q.

M365 Commercial Cloud is guided to +17% y/y at constant currency, or +18% adjusted for non-recurring revenue recognition benefits, 2pt above initial guidance under the old structure. Drivers are GitHub Copilot's move to consumption pricing, M365 Copilot (>30mn paid seats at FY26 exit, up >2x in two quarters), E5/E7 upgrades and price increases effective July 1.
DB models stable +23% y/y at constant currency for Agents & Infra through F2Q and F2H, and Azure no higher than the mid-40s, given capacity limits and the Rubin ramp.

Devices & Consumer: Windows OEM & Devices is guided to decline low-20s% on weak PC demand, component price increases, a tough comp and channel inventory drawdown. DB cites preliminary IDC data showing global PC shipments down about 20% y/y and 9% q/q.

Search/Ads ex-TAC guidance was raised mechanically to +MSD-HSD% after LinkedIn Marketing Solutions and Premium Subscriptions were added. Xbox Content & Services is guided to decline MSD%, and new cloud gaming hour limits start in November.

Re-segmentation moves GitHub cloud, other developer cloud services and Security Copilot from Azure to M365 Commercial Cloud, about $3bn of FY26 revenue growing >50% y/y. Azure plus M365 Commercial are about 75% of Agents & Infra revenue and DB expects 98% of segment growth over three years.
DB estimates the LinkedIn Marketing and Premium Subscriptions revenue now in Devices & Consumer at about $9.7bn in FY26, growing 16% y/y with an 85% gross margin.

Commercial RPO stood at $678bn at F4Q26. DB expects commercial cRPO growth in the mid-30s%+ versus mid-20s NTM consensus commercial revenue growth, and double-digit commercial bookings growth ex-OpenAI would be a solid outcome.

Capex including leases is guided above $50bn in F1Q. CY26 capex guidance was updated to $175bn from $190bn after the lease classification change. DB models FY27 capex of $215bn, near a roughly $220bn ceiling implied by the positive FCF commitment.
DB's FY27 estimates are revenue $389bn and non-GAAP EPS $19.47 (from $19.46). FY28 estimates are $460bn and $23.18. DB expects EPS compounding at a mid-teens%+ rate for several years.

Per DB, AI compute prices are up 40%+ in some cases from earlier in CY26, and new Azure AI business can likely be priced at higher margins than before, which supports Azure margin stabilization in FY27/28.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised from $550 to $600, about 28x FY27E non-GAAP EPS, after modeling the new segment structure. DB cites accelerating revenue growth with margin expansion and AI monetization across the stack.

sector_views.rationale: DB sees improving AI adoption and monetization at Microsoft and expects share gains within IT budgets.

earnings_insights: MSFT F1Q27 (DB estimate, not yet reported): revenue $90.4bn and non-GAAP EPS $4.71 versus Street (consensus estimate) at $90.7bn and $4.73.
MSFT F1Q27 revenue guidance midpoint is $90.4bn, about +17% y/y at constant currency. DB expects +18%-19% y/y at constant currency.

MSFT F2Q27 (DB estimate): revenue $95.2bn and non-GAAP EPS $4.76 versus Street (consensus estimate) at $96.1bn and $4.85. Consensus revenue is cited elsewhere as $95.7bn, or +18% y/y at constant currency.
DB expects F2Q27 gross margin of 65.7% (-2.3pts y/y) with upside potential. It models Agents & Infra at +23% y/y at constant currency and Devices & Consumer at -2% y/y.
FY27 DB estimates: revenue $389bn and non-GAAP EPS $19.47. FY28: $460bn and $23.18.
DB base case is that full-year operating margin guidance is maintained at down <1pt y/y, because the company has historically waited until F2Q results to pass through upside.
FX is expected to be a <1pt y/y headwind to revenue in both F1Q and F2Q27.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Weak PC demand from component price increases and inventory drawdown is a drag on Microsoft's Windows OEM & Devices line.

macro_indicators.reading: about 0.3% above prior quarter end and about 0.6% above the level when the company reported in late July
macro_indicators.interpretation: Implies a <1pt y/y FX headwind to revenue in F1Q and a similar one in F2Q27.

risk_factors: Increased competition for AI and public cloud.
Further deterioration of the macro environment.
Expectations for continued growth at large scale.
Compute capacity constraints ahead of the Vera Rubin ramp, a large backlog to service, and priority allocation to 1P Apps limit near-term Azure growth.
Unquantified benefit from the extended useful life of datacenter and building assets complicates margin interpretation.
Rising component costs and AI investment pressure gross margins.
Weak PC demand and price increases pressure Windows OEM, Xbox and other Devices & Consumer lines.
vol_and_positioning: Shares have climbed a further ~19% over the past several months after a strong T+1 move on last quarter's earnings, which DB reads as investors appreciating the combination of faster revenue growth and margin expansion.

tension_points.bull_case: GPU pricing is up 40%+ in some cases, efficiency gains raise monetization per asset, and agentic workloads use more CPU and ancillary software, which supports faster Azure growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Capacity constraints ahead of Vera Rubin, a large backlog and priority for 1P Apps limit Azure growth near term, so DB models no more than the mid-40s.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Little clarity on near-term capacity allocation beyond booked business, and a Rubin ramp that slips beyond F2H.

theme_stances.key_argument: Microsoft is showing AI monetization across its full stack, backed by enterprise incumbency.
theme_stances.evidence: tangible AI monetization across its full stack

theme_stances.key_argument: Component-driven PC price hikes and inventory drawdown pressure Windows OEM demand.
theme_stances.evidence: Windows OEM & Devices remains the primary drag
